output.answer: A new approach to talking about climate change, which links it to public health issues, was part of a roundtable discussion at Howard University's College of Medicine. During the discussion, Brian Deese, a senior adviser to the President, cited a recent study by the American Thoracic Society that found seven out of 10 doctors reported climate change is contributing to more health problems among their patients. The President also suggested that companies such as Google and Microsoft are developing apps which could allow families to monitor the air quality in their areas on a real-time basis. The World Health Organisation estimates climate change will cause an additional 250,000 deaths per year between 2030 and 2050, with the most likely cause of deaths being malaria, diarrhoea, heat exposure and under-nutrition.

However, according to the American Cancer Society (ACS), 1 total PSA levels between 4.0 ng/ml and 10.0 ng/ml may indicate prostate cancer, benign prostate hyperplasia (BPH), or inflammation of the prostate.

* The consideration for the lease is called rent.

8. Finally, dab this with a paper towel or cloth to remove excess paint.
9. Repeat these steps until you achieve the desired antique effect.

It is important to note that if you want a more realistic antique look, you can also use techniques such as sanding, distressing, or applying wax or varnish to your wood piece after painting.

output.answer: Louis Jordan, a 37-year-old unemployed truck driver from Conway, South Carolina, was rescued after drifting at sea for 66 days. He departed on his 35-foot Pearson sailboat, the "Angel," to fish but encountered a storm just days into the trip that capsized the vessel, broke its mast, and fractured his shoulder. Unable to repair the boat immediately, Jordan rigged a makeshift mast and survived by collecting rainwater when conditions allowed and catching fish attracted to his laundry. The boat capsized two more times during the ordeal. He was spotted by the crew of the container ship Houston Express hundreds of miles from land. Upon rescue, Jordan was found in surprisingly good condition, able to walk into Sentara Norfolk General Hospital. Coast Guard officials verified his story, noting his father reported him missing on January 29. Neighbors described him as a private man who loved his boat; he had slipped away while asking a neighbor to buy coffee creamer. Jordan credited his survival to his strong constitution and faith.

output.answer: A new approach to talking about climate change, which links it to public health issues, was part of a roundtable discussion at Howard University's College of Medicine. During the discussion, Brian Deese, a senior adviser to the President, cited a recent study by the American Thoracic Society that found seven out of 10 doctors reported climate change is contributing to more health problems among their patients. The President also suggested that companies such as Google and Microsoft are developing apps which could allow families to monitor the air quality in their areas on a real-time basis. The World Health Organisation estimates climate change will cause an additional 250,000 deaths per year between 2030 and 2050, with the most likely cause of deaths being malaria, diarrhoea, heat exposure and under-nutrition.

However, according to the American Cancer Society (ACS), 1 total PSA levels between 4.0 ng/ml and 10.0 ng/ml may indicate prostate cancer, benign prostate hyperplasia (BPH), or inflammation of the prostate.

* The consideration for the lease is called rent.

8. Finally, dab this with a paper towel or cloth to remove excess paint.
9. Repeat these steps until you achieve the desired antique effect.

It is important to note that if you want a more realistic antique look, you can also use techniques such as sanding, distressing, or applying wax or varnish to your wood piece after painting.

Step 1: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

Step 2: Season the beef tenderloin steak(s) as desired.

Step 3: Place the steak(s) in a large skillet and heat olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear the steak(s) for 1 minute.

Step 4: Place the entire skillet in the preheated oven and cook for about 5 minutes.

output.answer: The main difference between an S corporation and a C corporation is the taxation structure. S corporations are treated as pass-through entities, meaning that the company's profits and losses are passed through to the shareholders, who report them directly on their personal income tax returns. C corporations, on the other hand, are taxed separately from their shareholders, with the company paying taxes on its profits and the shareholders paying taxes on their dividends. Additionally, S corporations are required to file paperwork with the IRS to elect this status, while C corporations do not have this requirement.

output.answer: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) reported that a harmful pesticide, methyl bromide, was detected in a luxury villa at the Sirenusa resort in St. John, U.S. Virgin Islands, where a Delaware family of four fell ill last week. The family rented the unit from March 14 to March 22 and were later hospitalized. Methyl bromide is restricted in the U.S. due to acute toxicity and is prohibited for indoor use. Preliminary results confirmed its presence in the unit. The EPA is investigating whether the illness resulted from a fumigation on March 18 and if regulations were violated. Sea Glass Vacations stated their unit was not treated but licensed Terminix for pest control. The U.S. Department of Justice has initiated a criminal investigation based on an SEC filing by ServiceMaster Global Holdings, Terminix's parent company, which described the injuries as serious.

Sure, I'd be happy to help! Based on the given passages, here's how to play Farkle Ten:

1. Each player takes turns rolling the six dice.
2. If no point dice appear (i.e., if none of the dice show a 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6), a Farkle occurs and the player loses all the point dice they have collected during that turn.
3. If a player decides not to risk rolling a Farkle, they can stop rolling and the next player to the left goes.
4. Points are recorded on a scratch paper, but only if the player chooses to stop rolling without a Farkle.
5. The objective of the game is to have the highest score after 10 rounds of play.

There are special point values for certain combinations of dice rolls, as follows:

* Three of a kind: 2,500 points
* Four of a kind: 1,000 points (or double the three of a kind value, or quadruple the three of a kind value)
* Five of a kind: 2,000 points (or triple the three of a kind value, or six times the three of a kind value)

I hope that helps! Let me know if you have any further questions.

First, it incorrectly states 'If no point dice appear (i.e., if none of the dice show a 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6)' — but all standard dice only show 1–6; passage 2 defines a Farkle as 'no point dice appear', not 'no numbers appear', and the passages never define which faces are scoring (e.g., 1s and 5s typically score in classic Farkle, but that is not stated here). Second, it misattributes 'Three of a kind: 2,500 points' — passage 3 says 'Two sets of three of a kind: 2,500 points', not a single three-of-a-kind. Third, it omits that passage 3 gives ambiguous, non-exclusive scoring options (e.g., 'or double... or quadruple...') rather than definitive values, yet presents them as fixed rules. Fourth, it falsely implies Tostitos® Chips and salsa are part of gameplay mechanics (passage 2 mentions it humorously, not as a rule).

C corporations, on the other hand, are taxed separately from their shareholders, with the company paying taxes on its profits and the shareholders paying taxes on their dividends. Additionally, S corporations are required to file paperwork with the IRS to elect this status, while C corporations do not have this requirement.

output.answer: The 'end of an era' for the drama series "Mad Men" begins Sunday, marking the conclusion of a show set in the 1960s that has become part of the national fabric over eight years. The series, about a fictional advertising agency and its collision with changing times, spawned fashion lines, cocktails, museum exhibits, and presidential references. Don Draper, played by Jon Hamm, has become a symbol of the times. The previous season ended with the moon landing in July 1969, and the new season is expected to pick up soon after, potentially covering events like the Manson murders, Woodstock, and the Vietnam War moratorium demonstrations. Creator Matthew Weiner has remained tight-lipped about the finale. The show generally reflects disintegration, as old orders fall apart: white-shoe firms give way to ethnic pace-setters, New York is replaced by Los Angeles, and the "Good War" generation clashes with the "Make Love, Not War" cohort. 3. If a player decides not to risk rolling a Farkle, they can stop rolling and the next player to the left goes.

* Three of a kind: 2,500 points
* Four of a kind: 1,000 points (or double the three of a kind value, or quadruple the three of a kind value)
* Five of a kind: 2,000 points (or triple the three of a kind value, or six times the three of a kind value)

output.answer: The main difference between an S corporation and a C corporation is the taxation structure. S corporations are treated as pass-through entities, meaning that the company's profits and losses are passed through to the shareholders, who report them directly on their personal income tax returns. C corporations, on the other hand, are taxed separately from their shareholders, with the company paying taxes on its profits and the shareholders paying taxes on their dividends. Additionally, S corporations are required to file paperwork with the IRS to elect this status, while C corporations do not have this requirement.

output.answer: Richard Carlson was the son of an attorney and initially aspired to be an academic. He received his M.A. from the University of Minnesota and briefly taught there before working in theater as an actor, director, and writer. Early in his career, he was typecast as a diffident juvenile, making it difficult for him to land more mature roles; he tended to appear in monster flicks and B-movies in the '50s. In that decade, he turned to directing, beginning with Riders to the Stars (1954), which he also wrote and acted in. After several years of indifferent acting parts, he found renewed energy for his third-billed appearance in MGM's lavish Technicolor remake of King Solomon's Mines (1950).

The incident occurred about half an hour before landing. Minatel forced the cord down and was assisted by other passengers. Upon arrival at Hartsfield airport, U.S. authorities escorted the suspect off the plane. An FBI spokesman confirmed the man was transported for medical and mental evaluation under the direction of the Atlanta Police Department. No federal charges are currently pending as facts are being relayed to the U.S. Attorney's Office.

Speculation suggests characters like Roger Sterling, Ken Cosgrove, Harry Crane, and Joan Harris may exit, while Peggy Olson might head her own agency. A possible ending scenario involves Don Draper reflecting on the 1970 ban of cigarette ads on April 1st before leaving the show alone.

output.answer: The final season of "Mad Men" begins Sunday, marking the end of an era for the show about a 1960s advertising agency. Over eight years, the series became culturally significant, inspiring fashion lines, cocktails, and museum exhibits, though it was never a massive ratings hit. Don Draper, played by Jon Hamm, has become a symbol of the times. The previous season ended with the July 1969 moon landing, and the new season is expected to cover late-1960s events like the Manson murders, Woodstock, and Vietnam War demonstrations. The show reflects the disintegration of old orders, such as white-shoe firms giving way to ethnic agencies and New York being replaced by Los Angeles. Following a merger and the death of Bert Cooper, characters like Ken Cosgrove, Harry Crane, Joan Harris, and Roger Sterling face uncertain futures. Peggy Olson may start her own agency or marry, while Betty struggles with identity and Sally rebels. Speculation suggests the finale will occur on April 1, 1970, when Nixon bans cigarette ads, prompting Don to leave the show alone and on top of the zeitgeist.

output.answer: A passenger on an Air Canada flight from Toronto to Atlanta attempted to choke another passenger with a cord, possibly from headphones. The incident occurred about half an hour before landing. The victim, professional soccer player Oliver Minatel, forced the cord down and other passengers helped him. The suspect was not restrained but told to stay seated; he tried to stand up multiple times until passengers yelled at him. Upon landing in Atlanta, U.S. authorities escorted the suspect off the plane. An FBI spokesman confirmed the agency responded, noting the passenger was transported for medical and mental evaluation under the direction of the Atlanta Police Department. No federal charges are currently pending. Minatel's team expressed gratitude for the help received.

output.answer: The main difference between an S corporation and a C corporation is the taxation structure. S corporations are treated as pass-through entities, meaning that the company's profits and losses are passed through to the shareholders, who report them directly on their personal income tax returns. C corporations, on the other hand, are taxed separately from their shareholders, with the company paying taxes on its profits and the shareholders paying taxes on their dividends. Additionally, S corporations are required to file paperwork with the IRS to elect this status, while C corporations do not have this requirement.

best_candidate.answer: The main difference between an S corporation and a C corporation is the taxation structure. S corporations are treated as pass-through entities, meaning that the company's profits and losses are passed through to the shareholders, who report them directly on their personal income tax returns. C corporations, on the other hand, are taxed separately from their shareholders, with the company paying taxes on its profits and the shareholders paying taxes on their dividends. Additionally, S corporations are required to file paperwork with the IRS to elect this status, while C corporations do not have this requirement.

output.answer: Price is the amount of money you pay for a product or service, such as buying a book for $14.95 or getting your car detailed for $80. output.answer: The United States Department of Justice has indicted FedEx, a courier delivery service, with a 15-count indictment that includes charges of conspiracy, transportation of prescription pharmaceuticals with illegal prescriptions, violations of the Controlled Substances Act, misbranding, and money laundering. output.answer: The final season of "Mad Men" begins Sunday, marking the end of an era for the show about a 1960s advertising agency. Over eight years, the series became part of the national fabric with fashion lines, cocktails, and museum exhibits, though it was never a huge ratings hit. Don Draper (Jon Hamm) has become a symbol of the times. The previous season ended with the July 1969 moon landing; the new season is expected to pick up soon after, likely covering late-1969 events like the Manson murders, Woodstock, and Vietnam War demonstrations rather than jumping ahead. The show reflects the disintegration of old orders, such as white-shoe firms giving way to ethnic pace-setters and New York being replaced by Los Angeles. Following the merger with McCann Erickson and the loss of Bert Cooper, characters like Ken Cosgrove, Harry Crane, Joan Harris, and Roger Sterling may exit; Roger's health issues suggest a sudden departure. Peggy Olson might leave to head her own agency or marry. Betty struggles with identity, while daughter Sally rebels. A possible finale scenario places Don on April 1, 1970, watching Nixon ban cigarette ads, leaving him alone on top of the zeitgeist.

The case highlights the challenges of prosecuting corporations and the role of money and power in such cases.

The case raises questions about whether a corporation can be held criminally liable for "possessing" drugs that are sent through its service. FedEx argues that it is a common carrier and therefore cannot be held liable for possession, as it is simply providing transportation services to the public without discretion. The case highlights the challenges of prosecuting corporations and the role of money and power in such cases.

output.answer: After two months on the run, escaped Virginia inmate Naseem Roulack was captured by U.S. Marshals and Fairfax County Police on October 25. The 21-year-old, also known as Lil Nas, escaped on August 12 from Bon Secours St. Mary's Hospital in Henrico while seeking treatment. An investigation revealed he wore nylon flex cuffs because metal leg restraints were not reapplied after an MRI, and two corrections officers who admitted to sleeping resigned. Following his escape, Roulack was implicated in a Maryland carjacking and kidnapping, leading to a $20,000 reward. He was serving a 13-year sentence for aggravated malicious wounding, grand larceny, and hit-and-run.

In 1937-1938, he directed and co-wrote a production at the Hudson Theatre.

A proposed ending places Don Draper on April 1, 1970, watching Nixon ban cigarette ads, leaving him alone on top of the zeitgeist.

output.answer: The final season of "Mad Men" begins Sunday, concluding an eight-year run about a 1960s advertising agency and its collision with changing times. output.answer: To set up signatures in Outlook, open Outlook and click the File tab. Click Options in the menu list on the left side of the Account Information screen. On the Outlook Options dialog box, click Mail in the list of options on the left side of the dialog box. On the Mail screen, click Signatures in the Compose messages section. Click New under the Select signature to edit box on the Signatures and Stationery dialog box. A dialog box displays asking for a name for this signature. Enter a descriptive name in the edit box and click OK. Alternatively, start a new email in Outlook, click the Signature button and choose Signatures from the menu. Click New and enter a name for your signature. Save the signature. Another method is to select Tools | Options... from the menu in Outlook, go to the Mail Format tab, click Signatures... under Signatures, click New..., and give the new signature a name.

output.answer: The main difference between an S corporation and a C corporation is the taxation structure. S corporations are treated as pass-through entities, meaning that the company's profits and losses are passed through to the shareholders, who report them directly on their personal income tax returns. C corporations, on the other hand, are taxed separately from their shareholders, with the company paying taxes on its profits and the shareholders paying taxes on their dividends. Additionally, S corporations are required to file paperwork with the IRS to elect this status, while C corporations do not have this requirement.

output.answer: The final season of the critically acclaimed drama series "Mad Men" premieres on Sunday, marking the end of an era for the show set in the 1960s. The show, which has become a part of the national fabric, follows the lives of the employees of a fictional advertising agency and their personal struggles as they navigate the tumultuous decade. The finale is expected to wrap up loose ends and provide closure for the characters, with speculation that the show may tackle events such as the Manson murders, Woodstock, and the Vietnam War moratorium demonstrations. Creator Matthew Weiner has remained tight-lipped about the finale, leaving fans guessing about what will happen to the characters they have come to know and love.

Over eight years, the series became culturally significant despite modest ratings, inspiring fashion lines, cocktails, and even a bench in New York honoring its fictional headquarters. While creator Matthew Weiner remains tight-lipped, the new season is expected to pick up shortly after the previous season's conclusion with the July 1969 moon landing. Speculation suggests the show will cover late-1960s events like the Manson murders, Woodstock, and Vietnam War demonstrations rather than jumping ahead. The narrative reflects the decade's disintegration, featuring office turmoil following a merger and the departure of key figures like Bert Cooper. Predictions include potential exits for characters such as Roger Sterling, who faces health issues, and Joan Harris, while Peggy Olson may launch her own agency. Don Draper's arc might conclude with him reflecting on his past during the April 1970 ban on cigarette ads, leaving the show alone on top of the zeitgeist.

output.answer: The final season of "Mad Men" begins Sunday, marking the end of an era for the show about a 1960s advertising agency. Over eight years, the series became part of the national fabric with fashion lines, cocktails, and museum exhibits, though it was never a huge ratings hit. Don Draper (Jon Hamm) has become a symbol of the times. The previous season ended with the July 1969 moon landing; the new season is expected to pick up soon after, likely covering late-1969 events like the Manson murders, Woodstock, and Vietnam War demonstrations rather than jumping ahead. The show reflects the disintegration of old orders, such as white-shoe firms giving way to ethnic pace-setters and New York being replaced by Los Angeles. Following an ill-fitting merger and the departure of Bert Cooper, the agency is now owned by McCann Erickson. Speculation suggests characters like Ken Cosgrove, Harry Crane, Joan Harris, and Roger Sterling may exit, while Peggy Olson might head her own agency. The article concludes with a guess that the finale will occur on April 1, 1970, when Nixon bans cigarette ads, leaving Don alone.

output.answer: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) reported that a Delaware family of four fell ill after staying at a luxury villa in the U.S. Virgin Islands where methyl bromide, a restricted pesticide, was detected. The family rented the Sirenusa resort unit from March 14 to 22 and were hospitalized; the illness was reported on March 20. Preliminary results confirmed the presence of methyl bromide, which is prohibited indoors due to acute toxicity. The EPA is investigating whether a fumigation on March 18 caused the exposure and if regulations were violated. Sea Glass Vacations stated their unit was not treated but licensed Terminix for pest control elsewhere. The U.S. Department of Justice has initiated a criminal investigation based on an SEC filing by Terminix's parent company, which described the injuries as serious.

output.answer: The United States Department of Justice has indicted FedEx, a courier delivery service, with a 15-count indictment that includes charges of conspiracy, transportation of prescription pharmaceuticals with illegal prescriptions, violations of the Controlled Substances Act, misbranding, and money laundering. The charges stem from FedEx's alleged involvement in delivering drugs to dealers and addicts, despite warnings from its couriers and senior management about suspicious drug activity. The case raises questions about whether a corporation can be held criminally liable for "possessing" drugs that are sent through its service. FedEx argues that it is a common carrier and therefore cannot be held liable for possession, as it is simply providing transportation services to the public without discretion. The case highlights the challenges of prosecuting corporations and the role of money and power in such cases.

output.answer: The final season of "Mad Men" begins Sunday, marking the end of an era for the show about a 1960s advertising agency. Over eight years, the series became part of the national fabric, inspiring fashion lines, cocktails, museum exhibits, and even presidential references. Don Draper, played by Jon Hamm, has become a symbol of the times. The last season ended with the moon landing in July 1969, and the new season is expected to pick up soon after, potentially covering events like the Manson murders, Woodstock, and the Vietnam War moratorium demonstrations. Creator Matthew Weiner remains tight-lipped about the finale. The show reflects the disintegration of old orders, such as white-shoe firms giving way to ethnic pace-setters. Character fates remain uncertain; Roger Sterling might face a sudden departure due to health issues, while Peggy Olson may head her own agency. Betty Draper struggles with identity, and daughter Sally rebels. A possible ending scenario involves Don witnessing Nixon ban cigarette ads in April 1970, leaving the show alone on top of the zeitgeist.

output.answer: The main difference between an S corporation and a C corporation is the taxation structure. S corporations are treated as pass-through entities, meaning that the company's profits and losses are passed through to the shareholders, who report them directly on their personal income tax returns. C corporations, on the other hand, are taxed separately from their shareholders, with the company paying taxes on its profits and the shareholders paying taxes on their dividends. Additionally, S corporations are required to file paperwork with the IRS to elect this status, while C corporations do not have this requirement.

* Four of a kind: 1,000 points (or double the three of a kind value, or quadruple the three of a kind value)
* Five of a kind: 2,000 points (or triple the three of a kind value, or six times the three of a kind value)

I hope that helps! Let me know if you have any further questions.

A passenger on an Air Canada flight from Toronto to Atlanta attempted to choke another passenger with a cord from his headphones. The incident occurred about an hour before landing and the suspect was not restrained for the rest of the flight. The victim, a professional soccer player, was able to force the cord down and other passengers helped him. The suspect was escorted off the plane by authorities and is currently undergoing medical and mental evaluation. The soccer team the victim was traveling with released a statement expressing gratitude for the help of other passengers and relief that the victim is okay.

output.answer: The final season of "Mad Men" premieres Sunday, marking the end of an era for the show set in the 1960s. Over eight years, the series about a fictional advertising agency has become part of the national fabric, inspiring fashion lines, cocktails, and museum exhibits. While never a huge ratings hit, its cultural impact is evident, with Don Draper becoming a symbol of the times. The finale carries risks, recalling divided reactions to "The Sopranos" versus the acclaim for "Breaking Bad." Picking up after the July 1969 moon landing, the story may explore late-1969 events like the Manson murders, Woodstock, and Vietnam War demonstrations. The show reflects societal disintegration: old WASP firms yielding to new competitors, New York giving way to Los Angeles, and technological shifts. Following a turbulent merger, the agency now operates under McCann Erickson without Bert Cooper. Characters like Ken Cosgrove, Harry Crane, Joan Harris, and possibly Roger Sterling may depart. Peggy Olson's star continues rising, potentially leading her to start her own agency. Meanwhile, Betty Draper struggles with identity, and daughter Sally rebels. A speculative ending suggests April 1, 1970, with Nixon banning cigarette ads, leaving Don Draper alone yet atop the zeitgeist.

The pesticide is restricted in the US due to its acute toxicity, and its use indoors is prohibited. The family had rented the villa from 14-22 March and were later hospitalised. The EPA is working with local government agencies to investigate whether the family’s illness was caused by a fumigation at the resort on 18 March, and whether any environmental regulations were violated. The US Department of Justice has initiated a criminal investigation into the matter.

output.answer: The United States Department of Justice has indicted FedEx, a courier delivery service, with a 15-count indictment that includes charges of conspiracy, transportation of prescription pharmaceuticals with illegal prescriptions, violations of the Controlled Substances Act, misbranding, and money laundering. The charges stem from FedEx's alleged involvement in delivering drugs to dealers and addicts, despite warnings from its couriers and senior management about suspicious drug activity. The case raises questions about whether a corporation can be held criminally liable for "possessing" drugs that are sent through its service. FedEx argues that it is a common carrier and therefore cannot be held liable for possession, as it is simply providing transportation services to the public without discretion. The case highlights the challenges of prosecuting corporations and the role of money and power in such cases.

The final season of "Mad Men" premieres Sunday, marking the end of an era for the show about a 1960s advertising agency. Over eight years, the series became part of the national fabric, inspiring fashion lines, cocktails, and museum exhibits, with Don Draper symbolizing the times. While not a huge ratings hit, its cultural impact is evident, including a bench unveiled at New York's Time & Life Building. The new season, picking up after the July 1969 moon landing, will likely cover late 1969 events like the Manson murders, Woodstock, and Vietnam War demonstrations. The show reflects the disintegration of old orders, with Sterling Cooper now owned by McCann Erickson following a turbulent merger. Characters like Ken Cosgrove, Harry Crane, Joan Harris, and possibly Roger Sterling may seek exits due to office instability and personal issues. Conversely, Peggy Olson's star continues to rise, potentially leading her to start her own agency. Betty Draper struggles with identity, while her daughter Sally rebels as a teenager. The article speculates the series could conclude on April 1, 1970, with Nixon banning cigarette ads, leaving Don Draper alone atop the zeitgeist, unable to accept his past.

output.answer: On Air Canada Flight 8623 from Toronto to Atlanta, Oliver Minatel, a 22-year-old Brazilian soccer player, was choked by a stranger using a headphone cord about 30 minutes before landing. Minatel forced the cord down as passengers intervened; the suspect claimed the team intended to kill him. Though unrestrained, crew ordered him seated while passengers prevented him from standing. Upon arrival at Hartsfield Airport around 4:30 p.m., U.S. authorities escorted the suspect off for medical and mental evaluation under Atlanta Police coordination. The FBI confirmed involvement but stated no federal charges are pending yet. Minatel's Ottawa Fury FC coach expressed gratitude for the assistance and relief that Minatel is safe to play.

output.answer: The U.S. Department of Justice has indicted FedEx on 15 federal counts, including conspiracy, transporting pharmaceuticals via illegal prescriptions, Controlled Substances Act violations, misbranding, and money laundering. The indictment alleges that since at least 2004, FedEx knowingly delivered controlled substances from illegal internet pharmacies to dealers and addicts, despite internal safety concerns raised by couriers in Kentucky, Tennessee, and Virginia. FedEx maintains its innocence, arguing it qualifies as a "common carrier" exempt from possession liability under the Controlled Substances Act and Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act when acting in the usual course of business. The company contends it merely transports property for the public without discretion regarding contents. The DOJ disputes this, asserting FedEx knew or should have known of specific suspicious activities. While corporations can be criminally prosecuted, FedEx argues extending liability to common carriers would create absurd results, akin to holding bus drivers liable for passengers' contraband. The case underscores tensions between enforcing drug supply chains and legal definitions of corporate possession, with potential outcomes ranging from dismissal to massive fines via deferred prosecution agreements rather than incarceration.

The case highlights the challenges of prosecuting corporations and the role of money and power in such cases.

FedEx maintains its innocence, arguing it qualifies as a "common carrier" exempt from possession laws when acting in the usual course of business. The company contends that holding carriers liable for unknown package contents would be absurd and legally unsound. While corporations can be prosecuted like individuals, they lack certain constitutional rights, making them easier targets for government fines and policy enforcement through deferred prosecution agreements. The author suggests that while targeting the drug supply chain is strategically noble, prosecuting FedEx may not make legal sense, as the company merely transports property for the public without discretion. Ultimately, FedEx faces potential massive fines rather than incarceration, with the case highlighting the complexities of corporate criminal liability.

Stella Mare's is a highly-rated French and American restaurant located at 50 Los Patos Way in Santa Barbara, CA. Operating Tuesday through Saturday from 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM, the establishment offers a romantic and classy ambiance, featuring an elegant indoor greenhouse with string lights and a fireplace. Amenities include free WiFi, outdoor seating, lot parking, takeout options, and reservation availability.

Customers praise the welcoming decor and accommodating service, noting staff flexibility for late arrivals and special celebrations like birthdays. The menu features classic hearty bistro fare, with standout dishes including tender lamb shank, lobster-topped deviled eggs, canard à l'orange, and filet mignon. Brunch visitors enjoy warm sourdough bread and mini blueberry muffins, though one reviewer noted undercooked egg whites in a Croque Madame. The beverage selection includes solid cocktails and wines. With affordable pricing and a cozy atmosphere suitable for families and groups, Stella Mare's is described as a beautiful, historic spot on the water that patrons are eager to revisit.

To set up signatures in Outlook, you can follow these steps based on the provided passages:

For newer versions (via File tab):
1. Open Outlook and click the 'File' tab.
2. Click 'Options' in the menu list on the left side of the Account Information screen.
3. In the Outlook Options dialog box, click 'Mail' on the left side.
4. In the Compose messages section, click 'Signatures'.
5. In the Signatures and Stationery dialog box, click 'New' under the 'Select signature to edit' box.
6. Enter a descriptive name for the signature in the dialog box and click 'OK'.

Alternatively, from a new email:
1. Start a new email in Outlook.
2. Click the 'Signature' button and choose 'Signatures' from the menu.
3. Click 'New' and enter a name for your signature.

For older versions (via Tools menu):
1. Select 'Tools' | 'Options...' from the menu in Outlook.
2. Go to the 'Mail Format' tab.
3. Click 'Signatures...' under Signatures.
4. Click 'New...'.
5. Give the new signature a name.

You can also set a signature as your default so Outlook enters it in every new message you create.

Sure, I'd be happy to help! Based on the given passages, here's how to play Farkle Ten:

1. Each player takes turns rolling the six dice.
2. If no point dice appear (i.e., if none of the dice show a 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6), a Farkle occurs and the player loses all the point dice they have collected during that turn.
3. If a player decides not to risk rolling a Farkle, they can stop rolling and the next player to the left goes.
4. Points are recorded on a scratch paper, but only if the player chooses to stop rolling without a Farkle.
5. The objective of the game is to have the highest score after 10 rounds of play.

There are special point values for certain combinations of dice rolls, as follows:

* Three of a kind: 2,500 points
* Four of a kind: 1,000 points (or double the three of a kind value, or quadruple the three of a kind value)
* Five of a kind: 2,000 points (or triple the three of a kind value, or six times the three of a kind value)

I hope that helps! Let me know if you have any further questions.

output.answer: The main difference between an S corporation and a C corporation is the taxation structure. S corporations are treated as pass-through entities, meaning that the company's profits and losses are passed through to the shareholders, who report them directly on their personal income tax returns. C corporations, on the other hand, are taxed separately from their shareholders, with the company paying taxes on its profits and the shareholders paying taxes on their dividends. Additionally, S corporations are required to file paperwork with the IRS to elect this status, while C corporations do not have this requirement.

output.answer: On Air Canada Flight 8623 from Toronto to Atlanta, Oliver Minatel, a 22-year-old Brazilian soccer player, was choked by a stranger using headphone cords about 30 minutes before landing. Minatel forced the cord down while passengers intervened; the suspect claimed the team intended to kill him. Though unrestrained, crew ordered him seated as travelers prevented him from standing. Upon arrival at Hartsfield airport around 4:30 p.m., U.S. authorities escorted the man off for medical and mental evaluation coordinated by Atlanta Police. The FBI confirmed response but noted no pending federal charges. Minatel's Ottawa Fury FC coach expressed gratitude for passenger aid and relief that Minatel remains ready to play against the Atlanta Silverbacks.

output.answer: The final season of "Mad Men" premieres Sunday, marking the end of an era for the show about a 1960s advertising agency. Over eight years, the series became part of the national fabric, inspiring fashion lines, cocktails, and museum exhibits, with Don Draper symbolizing the times. While not a huge ratings hit, its cultural impact is evident, including a bench unveiled at New York's Time & Life Building. The new season, picking up after July 1969's moon landing, will likely cover late 1969 events like the Manson murders, Woodstock, and Vietnam War demonstrations. The show reflects the disintegration of old orders: white-shoe firms giving way to ethnic pace-setters, New York replaced by Los Angeles, and generational clashes. Following a merger with McCann Erickson, the agency faces turmoil without Bert Cooper. Characters like Ken Cosgrove, Harry Crane, Joan Harris, and Roger Sterling may seek exits, while Peggy Olson might start her own agency. Betty Draper remains lost amid turmoil, and daughter Sally rebels. A speculative finale suggests April 1, 1970, with Nixon banning cigarette ads, leaving Don alone, unable to accept his past.

output.answer: The U.S. Department of Justice has indicted FedEx on 15 federal counts, including conspiracy, transporting pharmaceuticals via illegal prescriptions, Controlled Substances Act violations, misbranding, and money laundering. The indictment alleges that since at least 2004, FedEx knowingly delivered controlled substances from illegal internet pharmacies to dealers and addicts, despite internal safety concerns raised by couriers in Kentucky, Tennessee, and Virginia. FedEx maintains its innocence, arguing it qualifies as a "common carrier" exempt from possession liability under the Controlled Substances Act and Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act when acting in the usual course of business. The company contends it merely transports property for the public without discretion regarding contents. The DOJ disputes this, asserting FedEx knew or should have known of specific suspicious activities. While corporations can be criminally prosecuted, FedEx argues extending liability to common carriers would create absurd results, akin to holding bus drivers liable for passengers' contraband. The case underscores tensions between enforcing drug supply chains and legal definitions of corporate possession, with potential outcomes ranging from dismissal to massive fines via deferred prosecution agreements rather than incarceration.

output.answer: The United States Department of Justice has indicted FedEx, a courier delivery service, with a 15-count indictment that includes charges of conspiracy, transportation of prescription pharmaceuticals with illegal prescriptions, violations of the Controlled Substances Act, misbranding, and money laundering. The charges stem from FedEx's alleged involvement in delivering drugs to dealers and addicts, despite warnings from its couriers and senior management about suspicious drug activity. The case raises questions about whether a corporation can be held criminally liable for "possessing" drugs that are sent through its service. FedEx argues that it is a common carrier and therefore cannot be held liable for possession, as it is simply providing transportation services to the public without discretion. The case highlights the challenges of prosecuting corporations and the role of money and power in such cases.

output.answer: The U.S. Department of Justice has indicted FedEx on 15 federal counts, including conspiracy, transporting pharmaceuticals via illegal prescriptions, Controlled Substances Act violations, misbranding, and money laundering. The indictment alleges that since at least 2004, FedEx knew illegal internet pharmacies were using its services to distribute drugs, despite warnings from regulators, Congress, and internal safety concerns raised by couriers in Kentucky, Tennessee, and Virginia. FedEx maintains its innocence, arguing it qualifies as a "common carrier" exempt from possession liability under the Controlled Substances Act and Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act when acting in the usual course of business. The company contends it offers transportation to the public generally without discretion, unlike entities solely moving contraband. While corporations can be prosecuted like individuals—a practice approved by the Supreme Court for over a century—FedEx asserts extending liability to couriers ignorant of package contents is legally unsound. The DOJ seeks to force corporate cooperation in policing pharmaceutical supply chains, potentially extracting fines through deferred prosecution agreements. Critics question the legal logic of prosecuting inanimate entities that cannot be incarcerated, suggesting such actions may ultimately harm consumers through economic trickle-down effects rather than achieving justice.

Tupelo Junction Cafe is a local business located at 1218 State St, Santa Barbara, CA. It is a restaurant that offers a variety of cuisines including breakfast and brunch, American (Traditional), American (New), and Southern dishes. The cafe is known for its great food and has received an average rating of 4.0 stars from customers. 

Customers have mentioned positive experiences with the food, particularly praising the scrambles and the excellent cinnamon apple beignets. One customer mentioned that the crab bloody Mary was a little watery but still had good spice. 

The cafe is open from 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM on Mondays and from 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM from Tuesday to Sunday. It offers outdoor seating and takeout options. Additionally, it is suitable for groups and accepts reservations. 

The business has a parking garage and street parking available, but no validated parking or valet service. However, it is important to note that the cafe does not provide WiFi. 

While the majority of reviews are positive, one customer mentioned that the cafe has moved to Newport Beach, California, and is no longer operating in Santa Barbara. Another review from 2017 expressed disappointment and mentioned that the restaurant had closed down. 

Overall, Tupelo Junction Cafe is a popular local restaurant known for its delicious food and accommodating service.

To set up signatures in Outlook, you can follow these steps based on the provided passages:

For newer versions:
1. Open Outlook and click the File tab.
2. Click Options in the menu list on the left side of the Account Information screen.
3. On the Outlook Options dialog box, click Mail in the list of options on the left.
4. On the Mail screen, click Signatures in the Compose messages section.
5. Click New under the Select signature to edit box on the Signatures and Stationery dialog box.
6. Enter a descriptive name for the signature in the dialog box and click OK.

Alternatively, start a new email, click the Signature button, choose Signatures from the menu, click New, and enter a name for your signature.

For older versions (Outlook 2013, 2010, or 2007):
1. Select Tools | Options from the menu in Outlook.
2. Go to the Mail Format tab.
3. Click Signatures under Signatures.
4. Click New.
5. Give the new signature a name.

To set up signatures in Outlook, you can follow these steps based on the provided passages:

For newer versions (via File tab):
1. Open Outlook and click the 'File' tab.
2. Click 'Options' in the menu list on the left side of the Account Information screen.
3. In the Outlook Options dialog box, click 'Mail' on the left side.
4. In the Compose messages section, click 'Signatures'.
5. In the Signatures and Stationery dialog box, click 'New' under the 'Select signature to edit' box.
6. Enter a descriptive name for the signature in the dialog box and click 'OK'.

Alternatively (via Tools menu):
1. Select 'Tools' | 'Options' from the menu in Outlook.
2. Go to the 'Mail Format' tab.
3. Click 'Signatures...' under Signatures.
4. Click 'New...'.
5. Give the new signature a name.

You can also start a new email, click the 'Signature' button, choose 'Signatures' from the menu, click 'New', and enter a name. Once created, you can set a signature as your default so Outlook enters it in every new message.

To set up a signature in Outlook, you can follow these steps based on your version:

For newer versions (via File menu):
1. Open Outlook and click the "File" tab.
2. Click "Options" in the menu list on the left side of the Account Information screen.
3. In the Outlook Options dialog box, click "Mail" on the left.
4. Click "Signatures" in the Compose messages section.
5. Click "New" under the "Select signature to edit" box.
6. Enter a descriptive name for the signature and click "OK".

Alternatively, for Outlook 2007/2010 (via Tools menu):
1. Select "Tools" | "Options" from the menu.
2. Go to the "Mail Format" tab.
3. Click "Signatures" under Signatures.
4. Click "New" and give the signature a name.

You can also access signature settings by starting a new email, clicking the "Signature" button, and choosing "Signatures" from the menu, then clicking "New" to enter a name. Once created, you can set a signature as your default so Outlook enters it in every new message.

Sure, I'd be happy to help! Based on the given passages, here's how to play Farkle Ten:

1. Each player takes turns rolling the six dice.
2. If no point dice appear (i.e., if none of the dice show a 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6), a Farkle occurs and the player loses all the point dice they have collected during that turn.
3. If a player decides not to risk rolling a Farkle, they can stop rolling and the next player to the left goes.
4. Points are recorded on a scratch paper, but only if the player chooses to stop rolling without a Farkle.
5. The objective of the game is to have the highest score after 10 rounds of play.

There are special point values for certain combinations of dice rolls, as follows:

* Three of a kind: 2,500 points
* Four of a kind: 1,000 points (or double the three of a kind value, or quadruple the three of a kind value)
* Five of a kind: 2,000 points (or triple the three of a kind value, or six times the three of a kind value)

I hope that helps! Let me know if you have any further questions.

review.explanation: The candidate's answer fulfills the task by providing a brief explanation of how to play Farkle based on the passages. However, it contains unsupported and contradictory claims. First, it incorrectly states 'If no point dice appear (i.e., if none of the dice show a 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6)' — but all standard dice only show 1–6; passage 2 defines a Farkle as 'no point dice appear', and the passages never define which faces are scoring (e.g., 1s and 5s are traditional, but not stated here). This paraphrase misrepresents the evidence. Second, it falsely attributes 'Three of a kind: 2,500 points' to passage 3, but passage 3 says 'Two sets of three of a kind: 2,500 points', not a single three-of-a-kind. Third, it omits that passage 3 gives ambiguous, non-exclusive scoring options ('or double... or quadruple...'), but presents them as definitive values. Fourth, it adds 'next player to the left goes' — while passage 2 says 'play passes to the player to the left', the candidate rephrases it as an active instruction ('goes'), implying agency not in the source. Finally, the Tostitos® reference is trivially supported (passage 2), but the candidate omits its humorous, non-mechanical nature — however, that omission is not a grounding failure. The core failures are the unsupported definition of 'point dice' and the misattribution of 2,500 points to single three-of-a-kind.

Step 1: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

Step 2: Season the beef tenderloin steak(s) as desired.

Step 3: Place the steak(s) in a large skillet and heat olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear the steak(s) for 1 minute.

1. **Objective**: The player with the highest score in 10 rounds of play wins.
2. **Gameplay**: Each player takes turns rolling all 6 dice.
3. **Farkle**: A Farkle occurs when no point dice appear upon rolling. In this case, the player loses all point dice collected during that turn, no points are recorded, and play passes to the player to the left.

   - Five of a kind: 2,000 points (described as triple or six times the three of a kind value).

output.answer: The main difference between an S corporation and a C corporation is the taxation structure. S corporations are treated as pass-through entities, where taxation passes through to the company's owners, who report their share of profits and losses directly on their personal income tax return, resulting in only one level of taxation at the shareholder level. C corporations, also referred to as regular corporations, are automatically formed when a business decides to incorporate. Additionally, S corporations must file paperwork with the Internal Revenue Service (such as IRS Form 2553) to elect this status, which is not a requirement for C corporations.

output.answer: The main difference between an S corporation and a C corporation is the taxation structure. S corporations are treated as pass-through entities, where taxation passes through to the owners who report their share of profits and losses on their personal income tax returns, resulting in only one level of taxation at the shareholder level. In contrast, a C corporation (or regular corporation) is automatically formed when a business incorporates. Additionally, S corporations must file paperwork with the Internal Revenue Service, such as IRS Form 2553, to elect this status, which is not a requirement for C corporations.

output.answer: The main difference between an S corporation and a C corporation is the taxation structure. S corporations are treated as pass-through entities, where taxation passes through to the company's owners, who report their share of profits and losses directly on their personal income tax return; they only pay one level of taxation at the shareholder level. To choose S corporation status, paperwork such as IRS Form 2553 must be filed with the Internal Revenue Service. In contrast, a C corporation (also referred to as a regular corporation) is automatically formed when a business decides to incorporate and does not have this IRS filing requirement for its status. Owners of a corporation share its profits with all stockholders in the form of dividends.

output.answer: Google's popular real-time traffic app, Waze, uses GPS navigation and crowdsourcing to alert users to traffic jams, automobile accidents, and through its "traffic cop" feature, the presence of law enforcement. However, this feature has been criticised for allowing users to identify the locations of police officers and indicate whether their presence is "visible" or "invisible". Google, which acquired Waze in 2013 for a reported $1.1 billion, has refused to discuss the issue with organisations representing law enforcement. The National Sheriffs' Association, for example, has raised concerns about the potential for the app to be used to obstruct law enforcement and put the lives of police officers at risk. Perpetrators of domestic violence, gang members and narcotics dealers can all use Waze to find out about the presence of law enforcement in certain areas.

output.answer: Migrants from over 20 countries, including Eritrea, Syria, Somalia, and West African nations, are increasingly using Libya as a transit point to reach Europe. In 2014, more than 80% of these migrants headed for the Libyan coast. Motivations vary: Eritreans flee indefinite military service and repression; Somalis escape Al-Shabaab and clan warfare; Syrians have lost hope of returning home; and many West Africans seek economic opportunities despite selling all their possessions. The journey involves crossing deserts and mountains, risking kidnapping, robbery, and exploitation by smugglers. Some migrants pay up to $5,000 or travel in dangerous conditions, such as being locked in ship holds. Experts note that worsening instability in Africa and the Middle East, combined with closed routes to Israel and Saudi Arabia, has driven this surge. Additionally, existing migrants in Libya face violence and persecution, prompting some to attempt the sea crossing they never originally intended. Smuggling networks have become more organized, often charging for "packages" that include both land and sea travel.

output.answer: Migrants from over 20 countries, including Eritrea, Syria, Somalia, and West African nations, increasingly use Libya as a transit point to reach Europe. Driven by severe push factors such as authoritarian repression, indefinite military service, clan warfare, poverty, and conflict (e.g., Boko Haram in Nigeria), many view this route as their only option, especially as alternatives like Israel have become more difficult. In 2014, over 80% of migrants headed for the Libyan coast. The journey involves well-established smuggling routes across deserts and mountains, where travelers face kidnapping, robbery, extortion, and death; some pay up to $5,000 or survive on toothpaste. Smugglers often provide migrants with GPS devices but no navigational skills, leading to dangerous sea crossings where Africans are frequently locked in holds while Syrians may secure better positions. While Eritreans and Syrians comprised half the traffic last year, West Africans also seek economic opportunities, often misled by unrealistic expectations. The situation is complicated by Libya's instability, ISIS presence, and rising organized crime, prompting neighboring countries to build fences and increase security, though these measures offer little deterrence.

output.answer: Photographer Simon Brann Thorpe's new project "Toy Soldiers" seeks to challenge viewers' attitudes towards violence and war by presenting images of soldiers posed as green plastic figurines against the harsh landscape of Western Sahara. Through his use of landscape photography, Thorpe positions the soldiers as if they were toys, making it easier for viewers to empathize with them and question the glorification of war. The project draws attention to the ongoing conflict between Morocco and the Polisario Front, which has been fought for 40 years, with thousands of casualties. Despite its significance, the war has received little coverage outside the region. Thorpe spent five weeks working with the Polisario Front to construct platforms for his images and worked with 50 to 60 soldiers at a time. His goal with "Toy Soldiers" is to encourage readers to think critically about the consumption of violent images and how they impact society.

review.explanation: The candidate fulfills the task by providing a concise summary under 120 words that captures Thorpe's intent, method, location, subject (Polisario Front), and purpose. However, it contains unsupported claims: 'thousands of casualties' is not stated or implied in the evidence; the evidence says nothing about casualties. Also, 'making it easier for viewers to empathize with them and question the glorification of war' misrepresents Thorpe's stated aim — he describes enabling 'a visual metaphor from which a viewer develops their own emotional, physical and political response... when faced with the realization that the images do not contain toy soldiers but real soldiers', not empathy facilitation or anti-glorification. The evidence also does not say the project 'draws attention to the ongoing conflict... with thousands of casualties'.

issues.evidence: The source text states: 'The conflict in Western Sahara receives virtually zero coverage despite 2015 being the 40th anniversary of the outbreak of war there,' and mentions a ceasefire in 1991 and division of people into two camps, but never cites or implies casualty figures.

issues.claim: making it easier for viewers to empathize with them and question the glorification of war
issues.evidence: Thorpe is quoted saying his project enables 'the creation of a visual metaphor from which a viewer develops their own emotional, physical and political response to war and conflict, when faced with the realization that the images do not contain toy soldiers but real soldiers.' Nowhere does the source mention empathy facilitation or 'glorification of war'.

output.answer: Dr. Kristen Lindsey, a Texas veterinarian, faced severe backlash after posting a Facebook photo of herself holding an orange tabby with an arrow through its head, captioning it as her "first bow kill" and joking about a "Vet of the year award." While she claimed the cat was feral, an animal rescuer suggested it was likely "Tiger," a missing pet of an elderly couple; CNN could not confirm this. The incident caused outrage at Washington County's Animal Clinic, crashing their website and overwhelming phone lines. Despite Lindsey initially claiming she would not lose her job, the clinic fired her, covered her name on the marquee, and distanced itself from her actions. An investigation by the Austin County Sheriff's Office is underway, with potential charges pending. Alley Cat Allies offered a $7,500 reward for evidence leading to an arrest, though some customers defended Lindsey as a good vet who made a poor social media choice.

The app could facilitate crimes such as drunk driving evading checkpoints, domestic violence, and gang activity. Furthermore, Google executives have refused to discuss these safety concerns with organizations like the National Sheriffs' Association, which represents over 3,000 sheriff's offices.

output.answer: The trial of Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the surviving suspect in the Boston Marathon bombing, continues with the jury deliberating for over seven hours without reaching a verdict. Prosecutors presented a strong case against Tsarnaev, highlighting the horrors of the bombing and the devastating impact on the victims and their families. The jury heard testimony from bomb survivors and first responders, as well as graphic evidence of the bombing itself, including a video of the moment the bomb exploded and dismembered an 8-year-old boy. The prosecution also presented evidence of Tsarnaev's involvement in the bombing, including his own written manifesto which expressed jealousy of his brother for dying as a martyr and lashed out at US policies he claimed killed Muslims. While the defense argued that Tsarnaev was merely following his older brother, Tamerlan, who they claimed was the instigator, prosecutors maintained that both brothers were equally guilty partners in crime. The jury will now consider the 30 charges against Tsarnaev, including setting off weapons of mass destruction as an act of terrorism, and will decide whether he is guilty of at least one of the 17 capital counts. If convicted, the trial will proceed to a second phase to determine Tsarnaev's sentence.

* The intercostal muscles contract, causing the ribcage to expand.
* The diaphragm contracts, pulling downwards to increase the volume of the chest.
* Pressure inside the chest is lowered, allowing air to be sucked into the lungs.

When you breathe out (exhalation):

* The diaphragm relaxes and moves upward into the chest cavity.
* The intercostal muscles relax, reducing the space in the chest cavity.
* Air rich in carbon dioxide is forced out of the lungs and windpipe, and then out of the nose or mouth.

output.answer: Somali-Canadian sisters Iman and Siham Hashi, known collectively as Faarrow, are recording their debut album in Los Angeles. Born in Mogadishu, they fled to Canada as refugees in 1991 following the outbreak of war. Now based in LA via Atlanta, the duo is preparing to release an Afro-pop sound described as a fusion of pop, hip-hop, and rhythmic African percussion. Their album, largely written and produced by the sisters alongside actor-musician Elijah Kelley, is currently in the mixing phase under Warner Brothers Records. Influenced by artists like Michael Jackson and the Spice Girls, Faarrow combines their musical career with significant humanitarian efforts. Working as spokespersons for the UNHCR, they advocate for refugees, having headlined events at the Kennedy Center and the Nansen Awards. Additionally, they launched "Wish Creatively," a socially conscious fashion brand selling jewelry to fund sustainable income projects for women in Kenya and Somalia. The sisters view their success as a way to inspire their generation, proving that creative paths can effectively contribute to rebuilding Somalia without conforming to traditional expectations.

In contrast, Marco Rubio's logo drew criticism for being amateurish and unconsidered. However, voters yearn for authenticity, and mass marketing has become a staple of presidential campaigns. Consistency is key to Hillary's success in reframing her message and movement, and she must integrate her humble and empathetic relationship with voters into all elements of her communication while living it every day.

output.answer: Somali-Canadian sisters Iman, 25, and Siham Hashi, 27, known collectively as Faarrow, are finalizing their debut album in Los Angeles. output.answer: The article argues that the Obama administration's Clean Power Plan functions as an energy policy rather than a genuine carbon reduction plan due to its bias against nuclear energy. Although nuclear power generates over 60% of U.S. carbon-free electricity, the EPA's modeling for the plan assumes no new nuclear construction and the retirement of 96 out of 99 operating plants by 2050. These assumptions effectively phase out the industry, creating incentives for states to replace nuclear plants with natural gas, which could increase real-world emissions despite model projections showing reductions. This approach contrasts with previous EPA models for the Lieberman-Warner and Waxman-Markey bills, which projected significant nuclear expansion. The bias reportedly stems from adopting policy choices similar to California's Global Warming Solutions Act, limiting credit for nuclear and hydropower while assuming unrealistic longevity for renewables. Furthermore, President Obama's executive order on federal sustainability denies agencies emission reduction credits for existing nuclear energy, allowing them only for small modular reactors. The author contends that these actions contradict the administration's stated belief in human-driven global warming and its claim to support an all-of-the-above energy strategy, demonstrating a lack of seriousness regarding actual carbon reduction.

output.answer: Former Australia cricket captain and legendary broadcaster Richie Benaud has died at the age of 84. Recently treated for skin cancer, Benaud was described by Cricket Australia as the most famous Australian player after Don Bradman. A veteran of 64 Test matches, he was a record-breaking leg-spinner who never lost a series in his 28 Tests as captain. Inducted into the Sport Australia Hall of Fame in 1985, he spent over four decades with the BBC, becoming the voice of cricket for millions in Britain and Australia. His passing triggered global condolences, including from Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott, who ordered flags flown at half-mast, and British Prime Minister David Cameron. Tributes poured in from cricket legends like Shane Warne, who called him a mentor and "godfather of cricket," and Michael Clarke. Writers and peers praised his authoritative yet dignified commentary style, noting he set incredibly high standards both on and off the field. Born in 1930 in Penrith, New South Wales, Benaud remains an iconic figure who defined an era of the sport.

In Ravi Opi, 90% of the houses are currently uninhabitable, and although some are still standing, residents are too scared of aftershocks to move back inside. output.answer: The aftermath of Nepal's earthquake reveals devastating damage even near the capital. The main highway east of Kathmandu is cracked and fissured, slowing travel to Ravi Opi, a village 30 kilometers away, to nearly two hours. While relatively lucky compared to regions closer to the epicenter, Ravi Opi suffers greatly; a local official states 90% of houses are uninhabitable due to structural instability and fear of aftershocks. Residents like Maili Tamang, injured and homeless, survey the ruins of their lives. Her daughter-in-law was transported by motorbike to a distant missionary hospital after escaping collapsed rubble. Tragedy strikes deeper for Mahesh Koiraba, who lost his two-year-old daughter when their home collapsed. With little aid arriving, displaced families huddle in makeshift shelters amid falling rain, lacking food, clothes, and safety. Osminda Koirale expresses terror over the uncertain future and lack of government support. Powerful aftershocks continue to threaten survivors. While this area is accessible, remote villages reachable only on foot face even worse conditions with unknown casualties and no aid, highlighting the enormity of the recovery task facing Nepal.

output.answer: The article argues that the Obama administration's Clean Power Plan functions as an energy policy biased against nuclear power rather than a genuine carbon reduction plan. Although nuclear energy generates over 60% of U.S. carbon-free electricity, the EPA's modeling for the plan assumes no new nuclear construction and the retirement of 96 out of 99 operating plants by 2050. The author contends these assumptions create incentives for states to replace nuclear plants with natural gas, potentially increasing real-world emissions despite modeled reductions. This approach contrasts with previous EPA models for the Lieberman-Warner and Waxman-Markey bills, which projected significant new nuclear construction. The bias is attributed to the EPA adopting policy choices from California's Global Warming Solutions Act, limiting credit for nuclear and hydropower while assuming unrealistic longevity for renewables. Furthermore, President Obama's executive order on federal sustainability denies agencies emission reduction credits for existing nuclear energy, allowing them only for small modular reactors. Citing warnings from former NASA scientist James Hansen, the author concludes that ignoring nuclear power undermines climate goals and contradicts the administration's claimed commitment to an all-of-the-above energy strategy.

output.answer: Former Australia cricket captain and legendary broadcaster Richie Benaud has died at the age of 84. Recently treated for skin cancer, Benaud was described by Cricket Australia as the most famous Australian player after Don Bradman. A veteran of 64 Test matches, he was a record-breaking leg-spinner who captained Australia from 1958 to 1964 without losing a series, becoming the first to achieve a Test double of 2,000 runs and 200 wickets. Inducted into the Sport Australia Hall of Fame in 1985, he later spent over four decades with the BBC, becoming cricket's most impersonated broadcaster known for witty one-liners. His passing generated global condolences. Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott stated Benaud personified cricket's traditions and ordered flags flown at half-mast. Current captain Michael Clarke called him more than just a cricketer, while Shane Warne honored him as a mentor and the "godfather of cricket." Tributes also came from international figures including Imran Khan, Kumar Sangakkara, and British Prime Minister David Cameron. Writers and coaches praised his authoritative yet dignified commentary style, noting he set incredibly high standards both on and off the field.

output.answer: In Nepal's Kavre District, the earthquake's magnitude is evident in cracked highways east of Kathmandu, where fissures are filled with rubble to allow passage. The 30-kilometer journey to Ravi Opi now takes two hours. While relatively lucky compared to areas closer to the epicenter, 90% of houses in Ravi Opi are uninhabitable, with residents fearing aftershocks. Maili Tamang, 62, survived after her two-story home collapsed, injuring her leg; her daughter-in-law was transported by motorbike to a distant missionary hospital. Mahesh Koiraba lost his two-year-old daughter, Prati, digging through wreckage with his hands. Despite small landslides and locals clearing roads, little aid has arrived. Displaced families, including Osminda Koirale's group, huddle in makeshift shelters without government support, lacking food and clothes. Torrential rain and powerful overnight aftershocks have heightened fear and hampered recovery. While this region is only 90 minutes from the capital, remote villages reachable only on foot were hit hardest, with unknown human losses and no aid yet delivered.

The mission's innovative goal is landing the rocket's first stage upright on an autonomous drone ship in the Atlantic, an attempt never before succeeded; a January try ended in explosion. Musk aims to cut space access costs up to 100-fold through reuse, estimating a 50% success chance. Dragon will deliver over 4,300 pounds of supplies, including an espresso maker, dock days later, and return with 3,000 pounds of cargo for a Pacific splashdown. This marks SpaceX's sixth station mission.

output.answer: Richie Benaud, a former Australia cricket captain and legendary broadcaster, has died at the age of 84. Benaud played in 64 Test matches, never losing a series in his 28 Tests as captain, and was inducted into the Sport Australia Hall of Fame in 1985. He also had a successful career with the BBC as a commentator for over four decades. His insightful style was greatly appreciated by fans and players alike. News of his passing led to an outpouring of grief from figures such as Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott, who ordered flags to fly at half-mast, and cricket legends including Shane Warne and Michael Clarke.

Swedes cite lack of legal advantages and secular values as reasons to avoid formal marriage. Ultimately, while the author found commitment valuable for navigating life's challenges, the trend suggests marriage is becoming a choice based purely on love and practicality rather than social expectation.

output.answer: Night Lizard Brewing Company, located at 607 State St in Santa Barbara, CA, is a highly-rated brewery and restaurant offering Mediterranean cuisine and craft beer. With garage parking available and weekend hours extending until midnight, Night Lizard remains a top choice for those seeking a relaxed environment with solid brews.

output.answer: Peabody's is a bar and American traditional restaurant located at 1198 Coast Village Rd in Santa Barbara, CA. Ultimately, Peabody's offers a mixed experience dependent on service timing and menu selection.

output.answer:
To attach multiple picture frames together, you can use a couple of methods. One way is to use a stand grouping method where you select two or three frames of the same wood molding. For joining two frames, use identical frames. If you're joining three together, choose either three of the same or one which is larger to be the middle frame. Lay them beside each other to check the effect. Put two frames together back to back, and mark the hinge placement. The placement should be the same distance from the bottom edges of each frame to ensure that the grouped pictures stand securely on the table top. Attach two small hinges to the connecting sides of the frames. 

Another method involves screwing the frame to a backer board. Repeat this with each frame. Have the pictures all ready in the frames to save time. You can always unscrew them at a later date to change the picture if you want. Attach a hanging wire to the back, hang it up and step back to enjoy the results. 

If you're hanging multiple pictures together, it may be helpful to test ideas by laying the group of pictures out on the floor first.

Based on the provided passages, the main difference between ad hominem fallacy and poisoning the well fallacy is the timing of the attack.

Ad hominem fallacy occurs when an attack is made on a person's character, motive, or other attribute directly related to their argument, rather than attacking the argument itself. This type of attack can happen at any point during a debate or discussion.

On the other hand, poisoning the well fallacy involves making an ad hominem attack (i.e., attacking a person's character or integrity) before the merits of a case can be considered. In other words, it is an attempt to discredit a person's argument by attacking their personal integrity or intelligence before the discussion has even begun.

So, while both fallacies involve attacking a person's character rather than their argument, ad hominem fallacy happens after the argument has been presented, while poisoning the well fallacy happens before the argument is even presented.

The candidate's claim that ad hominem 'can happen at any point' is consistent with passages 1 and 2 (which do not specify timing), and their claim that poisoning the well occurs 'before the argument is even presented' is directly supported by passage 3's phrase 'before the merits of a case can be considered'. No unsupported or contradictory claims are made.

Ad hominem fallacy occurs when an attack is made on a person's character, motive, or other attribute directly related to their argument, rather than attacking the argument itself. This type of attack can happen at any point during a debate or discussion.

On the other hand, poisoning the well fallacy involves making an ad hominem attack (i.e., attacking a person's character or integrity) before the merits of a case can be considered. In other words, it is an attempt to discredit a person's argument by attacking their personal integrity or intelligence before the discussion has even begun.

So, while both fallacies involve attacking a person's character rather than their argument, ad hominem fallacy happens after the argument has been presented, while poisoning the well fallacy happens before the argument is even presented.
